mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discount rates reducing expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) while UNRATE falls suggests labor market strengthening, which precedes S&P 500 positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >70% of similar labor market tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (retail sales) accompanied by a decline in INDPRO (industrial production) indicates shifting demand composition toward services, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while INDPRO decreases in the current month
regime_hint: transition from industrial to services dominance
failure_condition: No significant correlation between HOUST/INDPRO shifts and S&P 500 20-day returns in analogous transitions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in INDPRO below 100 suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months during a low-inflation regime, it signals accommodative policy and tends to produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 255 over same horizon
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive (mean <= 0) in 3 consecutive low-inflation periods with similar policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in UNRATE above 8% in a tight labor market is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 8% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during comparable spikes.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (consumer demand) and PAYEMS (employment) over the next month predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return through stronger household and labor confidence.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and PAYEMS increases in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are flat or negative despite the signal in analogous expansionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below 500 million dollars in a consumer-weak regime predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to declining retail activity.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 500 in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during comparable consumer weakness episodes.
